column3: EQUIVALENT: _validated_binding (G-BD-CHANGES-DISTINCT) admits only DISTINCT binding change_ids, so a record list with a duplicate always has len(sorted(rec_changes)) != len(binding change_ids) and sub-clause #5 (sorted(rec_changes) != binding['change_ids']) refuses it on the same line with the same reason; no input reaches a different outcome

EQUIVALENT: only _admit_backfill builds non-live units and it always sets reviewer=None, so for every non-live unit sub-clause #2 (reviewer is not None) is already False; dropping the source test admits no additional unit into the reuse map

EQUIVALENT (round-4 reviewer's own classification): a string that is not 64 lowercase hex chars can never equal hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(), so G-E-HASH-MATCH#2 refuses it with the same (None, None); the early check only saves the open/read

EQUIVALENT (round-4 reviewer's classification of the self-citation guard): disabling the self-citation check can only let a record cite its OWN file, and a record cannot carry the sha256 of bytes that include that same hash (fixed point), so G-E-HASH-MATCH#2 refuses every self-citation with the same (None, None); a hardlink has a different realpath and meets the same impossibility

EQUIVALENT (unreachable on POSIX): os.path.commonpath raises ValueError only for a mix of absolute and relative paths or an empty sequence; both arguments are os.path.realpath() results, which are always absolute (even for '' or a relative input), so the handler can never run and replacing its body cannot change any outcome

EQUIVALENT: forcing this operand True leaves 'None == resolved_real' when own_real is None, which is False exactly as before (resolved_real is always a realpath string); and own_real is never None in practice because os.path.realpath does not raise OSError (non-strict)

EQUIVALENT: a whitespace-only citation strips to '' and resolves to os.path.join(base_real, '') = the citing record's own directory (always an existing directory inside --records); the O_RDONLY open of a directory succeeds, then G-E-REGULAR refuses it, and if that were absent the read raises IsADirectoryError which G-E-READ turns into the same (None, None) -- the outcome is identical whether or not #2 fires

EQUIVALENT (round-4 reviewer's own classification): a directory read raises and G-E-READ catches it; a FIFO with no writer reads b'' and G-E-HASH-MATCH#1 refuses it; a FIFO with a writer must deliver the hash-pinned bytes (no gain); a user-creatable socket fails to open (ENXIO, G-E-OPEN); devices cannot be created in the root without privilege and hardlinks cannot cross filesystems

EQUIVALENT (unreachable): non-strict os.path.realpath never raises OSError -- measured on this host's Python 3.13 for a symlink loop, a chmod-000 parent, and a missing path (all returned a string; control needle: a NUL byte DID raise, ValueError, so the probe could see exceptions); record_own_path comes from os.walk and never contains NUL, so the handler cannot run

EQUIVALENT: _lists only ever receives ADMITTED units, whose change_ids is always a list -- a live unit's is list(binding['change_ids']) (_admit_live) and a backfill unit's is its validated list or [] for "UNKNOWN" (_admit_backfill, G-B-CHANGES-SHAPE/DEFAULT) -- so the operand is True for every reachable input
EQUIVALENT: with this operand removed, None falls through G-NL-INT (not an int) and G-NL-STR (not a str) to the function's final 'return None' -- the same result the early return gives
EQUIVALENT: None is not an int, so sub-clause #3 (not isinstance(owner_uid, int)) fires for it with the same reason string; the explicit None test is redundant
EQUIVALENT: None is not an int, so sub-clause #3 (not isinstance(producer_uid, int)) fires for it with the same reason string; the explicit None test is redundant

EQUIVALENT: both callers pass only dicts -- cmd_record refuses a non-dict finding first (G-R-FINDING-SHAPE, exit 2) and evaluates finding.get('id') in the call's own label argument, and cmd_backfill (outside the guarded call graph) does the same finding.get('id') before the call -- so the operand is False for every input that reaches it
EQUIVALENT: for a dict without the key, finding.get('finding_layer') is None and the very next guard G-FL-NULL returns the same (None, None)

EQUIVALENT: FINDING_LAYERS is a TUPLE of three strings, so 'value in FINDING_LAYERS' compares by == and is True only for one of those exact strings; no non-str value (list, dict, int, bool) equals a str, and tuple membership never raises for an unhashable value -- the isinstance operand changes no result
EQUIVALENT: when the key is absent, verdict_doc.get('slice_verdicts') is None and sub-clause #2 returns the same (None, None)
EQUIVALENT: 'seen' is keyed only by string slice ids (G-SV-KNOWN-SLICE admits str only), so for sid None the second operand seen.get(None) == 'GO' is already False; the None test changes no result

EQUIVALENT: the outer location test is a fast path only -- the inner G-CF-MARKER-MATCH requires a non-empty str marker_file EQUAL to file_ and a non-None marker_line EQUAL to line_, so a non-str file_ can never equal a str marker_file; forcing this operand True therefore never yields 'false-positive' for an input the original classifies otherwise

EQUIVALENT: the outer location test is a fast path only -- the inner G-CF-MARKER-MATCH requires a non-empty str marker_file EQUAL to file_ and a non-None marker_line EQUAL to line_, so an empty file_ can never equal a non-empty marker_file; forcing this operand True therefore never yields 'false-positive' for an input the original classifies otherwise

EQUIVALENT: the outer location test is a fast path only -- the inner G-CF-MARKER-MATCH requires a non-empty str marker_file EQUAL to file_ and a non-None marker_line EQUAL to line_, so a None line_ can never equal a non-None marker_line; forcing this operand True therefore never yields 'false-positive' for an input the original classifies otherwise

EQUIVALENT: the same condition requires marker_file == file_, and the outer G-CF-LOCATED admits only a str file_; a non-str marker_file never equals a str, so dropping this operand admits no extra match

EQUIVALENT: the same condition requires marker_file == file_, and the outer G-CF-LOCATED admits only a non-empty file_; an empty marker_file never equals it, so dropping this operand admits no extra match

EQUIVALENT: the same condition requires marker_line == line_, and the outer G-CF-LOCATED admits only a non-None line_; a None marker_line never equals it, so dropping this operand admits no extra match

EQUIVALENT: the binding's change_ids are distinct (G-BD-CHANGES-DISTINCT), so a batch change list with a duplicate always has len(sorted(b_changes)) != len(binding change_ids) and G-R-BINDING-BATCH#3 (sorted(b_changes) != binding['change_ids']) refuses it with the same message and exit 1

EQUIVALENT: treating '.' as a lookup re-stats the current directory under the name cur/. (same inode, already in dirs and already checked for owner and ACL); the extra edge (cur, cur's own stat) refuses only for a foreign-writable directory that is non-sticky -- which the NEXT lookup in that same directory refuses too -- or sticky but owned by neither the owner nor root, which G-T-DIR-OWNED already refuses; a trailing '.' leaves the same directory leaf
EQUIVALENT: when the key is absent, verdict_doc.get('reviewer') is None and sub-clause #2 returns the same (None, None)
